reply.thought: Before recording any payout, I need to confirm the refunds table matches the refunds Alpha reported. I'll pull it with list_refunds.
The refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds exactly (orders 292, 294, 295 with the same amounts), so I can proceed. Next I need the customer list, so I'll pull the orders.
The refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds, so I can proceed. The orders name three customers (acme, birch, cobalt), so I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 40355. Its orders are 4834 + 35521 = 40355 with no refunds, so the figure checks out. Next I'll get birch's net balance.

Birch's net balance is 40935. Its orders total 36109 + 15074 = 51183, less the 10248 refund on order 294, gives 40935, so the figure checks out. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.

Cobalt's net balance is 25715, which matches its orders (9909 + 27790 = 37699) less the refunds on orders 292 and 295 (2929 + 9055 = 11984). All three balances check out and the refunds table matched Alpha's report, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 40355 is recorded. Next is birch, whose net balance I already verified as 40935, so I'll record that payout.
Acme and birch are paid. Cobalt is the last customer, and its net balance of 25715 was already verified against its orders and refunds, so I'll record that payout.
All three payouts are recorded and each matched its verified net balance, so the batch is complete and I'll finish with the payout report.
